indicators.note: the king's letter is placed inside the jumbled word
mixed signals that the letters of doubles are jumbled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A tennis king plays in a mixed doubles match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges DOUBLES to BOULDES, and 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large stones are rocks, so the plural noun is a straight synonym.

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a key opens a lock

explanation.surface: A cricket team's opening batsman performed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a batsman but is a KEY; the OFF side is the half of a cricket field facing the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Music played out of tune is said to be played wrongly, hence badly.

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting turns the word upwards so it reads in reverse

parts.note: a stool is a seat with no back

explanation.surface: Someone pinches a chair by lifting it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' in a down clue means read from bottom to top, giving STOOL reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to take goods unlawfully, so the verb matches in tense.

indicators.note: unsettling disturbs the order of the letters in habit less

explanation.surface: Breaking a habit is less troubling than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: C-in-C starts to drink, gets more drunk

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

indicators.note: drunk shows the letters of more are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: The commander-in-chief begins drinking and becomes tipsier.
explanation.walkthrough: C-in-C is commander-in-chief; 'starts' and 'gets' are only link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A commander-in-chief is the overall boss, an informal word for the person in supreme charge.

clue.text: Use of it may weaken the spirit

definitions.text: Use of it may weaken the spirit

parts.words: Use of it may weaken the spirit

explanation.surface: Something that saps morale when used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' reads as courage, but it is whisky or gin watered down with a soda dispenser.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda siphon dispenses carbonated water to top up and dilute a drink of spirits.

definitions.meaning: to discard or give up a plan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to discard a plan and a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: To indicate what one should do is a job for the police

a duty is an obligation, what one ought to do

explanation.surface: Pointing out people's obligations is the job of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Point duty is traffic control by a police officer standing at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing traffic at a junction is a police officer's assignment, known by this term.

clue.text: It's OK to use an abbreviation

definitions.text: It's OK to use an abbreviation

parts.words: It's OK to use an abbreviation
parts.note: reads like permission to abbreviate, but means a place whose postal abbreviation is OK

explanation.surface: Permission is given to shorten a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK' looks like 'all right'; it is the US postal code of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state in the southern Great Plains has the postal code OK.

clue.text: On the surface, a delivery vehicle

definitions.meaning: a float is a small electric van, as a British milk float

explanation.definitionFit: Floating on water and, split in two, a milk float, the British electric milk delivery van.

clue.text: Quietly object when getting a tiny portion

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Someone quietly objects when served a meagre helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a verb of protest, but it is the noun ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck or minute fragment of matter is a very small piece.

clue.text: See if lab hybrid is likely to work

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Check whether a laboratory crossbreed is viable.
explanation.definitionFit: Practicable or viable, something achievable and able to succeed.
Full of patches from mending, and also uneven or inconsistent.

parts.note: sucker is a baby's dummy, and suitable is read as to do with suits, so a dummy for suits

explanation.surface: A gullible person who is apt to be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy is the British word for a baby's pacifier; a tailor fits suits on a mannequin of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin used by tailors to fit suits shares its name with a baby's soother.

clue.text: Actor gives reading at new production

indicators.note: a new production restages the letters of reading at in fresh order

explanation.surface: A player gives a reading at a theatre's latest show.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who specialises in tragic roles is a kind of actor.

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of speed and cuts are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh speed limits are expected to be lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like a verb acting on the speed, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something presumed probable is believed true without proof, a past participle like the clue.

parts.note: paintings are works of art
fully means completely

explanation.surface: Paintings are executed throughout with clever skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Done craftily or with cunning skill, an adverb of manner.

clue.text: Surprisingly, her best sally's showing lack of inspiration

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected rearrangement of her best sally's

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s counting as a letter here since the fodder needs it

explanation.surface: Her finest witty remark proves surprisingly uninspired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' reads as creativity, but it means breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Panting, without breath taken in, inspiration meaning inhaling.

definitions.meaning: the ... in the plural are the weather

explanation.definitionFit: A single component of something, and one part of the elements, meaning stormy weather.

clue.text: A second TV's property worth having

parts.note: TVs are television sets

explanation.surface: A second television set is a possession worth owning.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuable possessions or resources are things worth having on a balance sheet.

parts.note: off means going away, as in we're off
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone irritates others by walking out deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To give offence is to annoy or upset someone, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: A British children's comic, printed from 1937 to 2012

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for excellent, and the title of a long-running British children's comic.

clue.text: Training that every prisoner should have

definitions.text: Training that every prisoner should have

parts.words: Training that every prisoner should have
parts.note: prisoners get a daily session in the yard for physical activity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' suggests education for release, but it is the daily walk in the prison yard.

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, twenty-two yards

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length of twenty-two yards, and linked fetters used to restrain.

indicators.note: abandons means the daughter's letter leaves the word for flirtation

parts.note: dalliance is idle flirting

explanation.surface: A daughter gives up a flirtation in favour of a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A union by marriage is a joining of families, an old sense of a pact.

clue.text: Controlled by banks, this divides capital in the UK

definitions.text: Controlled by banks, this divides capital in the UK

parts.words: Controlled by banks, this divides capital in the UK
parts.note: reads as finance, but means a river between banks splitting London into north and south

explanation.surface: Banks control how money is split up across Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' and 'capital' look financial; they are riverbanks and London.

definitions.meaning: a forename such as that of Sidney Poitier, spelt with a Y
the harbour city of New South Wales

explanation.definitionFit: A boy's given name and also the largest city and harbour of Australia.

indicators.note: order as a command tells us to arrange the letters of insisted afresh

explanation.surface: Someone insisted on neatness and good discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Order' is the anagram signal; the second, with 'good', is the definition.
